transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’ve been putting this off because I didn’t want to make it sound dramatic. But lately I’ve had some thoughts like, if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow, maybe that would be easier. I don’t want to hurt myself, I really don’t, but it scared me enough that I thought I should probably talk to someone.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m completely falling apart or anything. But most mornings lately I wake up with this kind of heavy, gray feeling, like the color’s already drained out of the day before I even get dressed for work. If that makes sense.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

I think so, yes. It’s been about two months now, maybe a little more or less, since things started getting difficult with the new district manager. I don’t want to blame everything on work, but that’s when this whole up-and-down thing with my mood and energy really seemed to start.
When you’re away from work, do you still feel depressed?

Yeah… I do, I think. It’s not only at work. Most mornings lately, even before I’m getting ready for the store, I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling—like the day’s already kind of drained of color. I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it, but… yes, it follows me outside of work too.
Have you been enjoying things you usually enjoy less than before?

A little, yes. I mean, I still try to do the things I normally like… I’ll set out my paints, or I’ll think, “Okay, go to pottery class, you’ll feel better once you’re there.” But then I get there and I just sort of stare at the materials. The spark I used to feel isn’t really there right now. I don’t know if that counts, but… it’s not quite the same.
Before this started two months ago, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for days or weeks at a time?

I… yes, I think so. I may have made it sound like it only began two months ago because work made it more obvious, but the flatter, low feeling has really been there longer—maybe about six months. Not every second, and I’ve been functioning, but things like my art classes or morning walks just haven’t really restored me the way they used to. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you felt this low mood more days than not for at least two years?

I don’t think so… not two years, no. I mean, I’ve had lower stretches here and there, like anyone, I suppose, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. The more consistent low mood is more recent than that. Is that the kind of distinction you’re asking about?
Have you noticed a change in your sleep lately?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed a big change, honestly. I mean, I have the occasional night where I don’t sleep as well, but I don’t know that it’s anything unusual. Should I be tracking that more closely?
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

I don’t think there’s been a major change. My appetite seems mostly the same, maybe a little up and down depending on the day, but nothing that’s really stood out to me. Should I be paying closer attention to that?
Before this current low period, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks in a row?

I’m not sure I can think of a clear time like that, no. I’ve had difficult patches, of course, but whether it was depressed like this for a full two weeks in a row… I don’t want to say yes if I’m not certain. I don’t think so.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?

A little, yes… not terribly, I don’t think, but I do notice I get kind of foggy with small decisions. Like at work, something that used to be automatic—choosing which endcap to reset first—can have me standing there second-guessing myself. Even picking out a blouse some mornings takes longer than it should. I don’t know if that counts as concentration exactly, but it’s been happening.
Lately, have you been feeling worthless or like you’ve been letting people down?

A little, yes… I mean, I know everyone makes small mistakes, and I’m probably being too hard on myself. But lately I’ll replay things from work, like if a display sign was crooked or one of the trainees looked confused after I explained something, and then I start thinking, “What kind of supervisor am I?” Sometimes it goes as far as feeling like I’m just useless at it, which I know sounds dramatic.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy lately?

Yes… a bit. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even if I’ve been in bed all night, I can feel sort of worn out by things that shouldn’t take much. Like opening the store, answering a few questions from staff, or just carrying groceries in from the car. It’s not that I can’t do them, but they seem to take more out of me lately. Does that make sense?
During this low period, have you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

I think… yes, in a mild way, if that makes sense. Most mornings lately I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling, like the color’s already drained out before I even get dressed for the store. I can still get myself going, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it has been there a lot of the day, most days.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual lately?

Maybe a little, yes. I don’t know if it would be noticeable to other people, exactly… but some days I catch myself sort of pacing around the living room or picking at my cuticles, like I can’t quite settle. And then other days, it’s the opposite—just walking from the break room to the sales floor feels strangely slow, like I’m moving through molasses. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you been worrying a lot lately, even about everyday things?

I don’t think so… not more than normal, anyway. I mean, I have the usual worries about work and keeping things running, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying all day about little things. At least, I don’t think that’s what’s been going on. Is that the kind of worry you mean?
Have you had any thoughts of actually killing yourself?

Not… not exactly. I don’t want to hurt myself. But I guess what scared me enough to come in is I’ve had thoughts like, if I didn’t wake up tomorrow, that might be easier. I feel a little ashamed saying that, because I don’t want you to think I’m being dramatic.
Have your low mood and hopeless thoughts been mainly caused by problems in a close relationship, like with a partner or spouse?

I don’t think so. I mean, no relationship is perfect, but I wouldn’t say this is mainly about my partner or anything like that. At least, it doesn’t feel like that’s the center of it. Is that what you’re asking?
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to function at work or in your daily life?

A little, yes… I mean, I’m still going to work, and I’m taking care of myself and the house and all that, so it’s not like I’ve completely fallen apart. But I have noticed I’m avoiding extra conversations with staff when I can, and I’ve been putting off even simple store decisions because I don’t really trust my judgment right now. I don’t know if that counts as “hard to function,” but it’s not quite like me.
Lately, have you often felt guilty or blamed yourself a lot?

Yes… I suppose I have. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I keep replaying these little things from work—like if a display sign was crooked, or if a trainee looked confused after I explained something—and then I start thinking, “What kind of supervisor am I?” Sometimes it turns into me telling myself I’m just useless at it, even though I know that’s probably not fair. Does that make sense?

opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a current depressive episode: depressed mood most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks, reduced interest/pleasure, low energy, impaired concentration/indecisiveness, excessive guilt/worthlessness, psychomotor change, passive death wishes, and functional impact. Although symptoms worsened in the context of a work stressor, the syndrome extends beyond the stressor, persists outside work, and is better characterized as a depressive episode than adjustment disorder.
